Clerk of the Circuit Court & Comptroller
Barbie Higginbotham, Clerk of the Circuit Court & Comptroller for Dixie County, Florida
was elected as the Clerk of the Circuit Court & Comptroller on November 2020. The Clerk of the Circuit Court is an elected office established according to the Florida Constitution for the purpose of serving the citizens of each county as a public trustee. As an elected official, the Clerk of the Circuit Court helps provide for the system of “checks and balances” that is the very foundation of the American form of government.

Strong financial oversight helps promote accountability, transparency, and responsible stewardship of public funds.

Meet the Clerk
For those of you who don’t know me, I am Barbara Higginbotham.
I am the daughter of Johnny and Martha Foster and grew up as a Navy brat, moving around every few years until my dad retired in 1983 and moved us to Dixie County to live near my grandparents. I am a proud 1985 graduate of Dixie County High School.
My husband and I (Daryle, aka “30”) have owned and operated a local home cooking restaurant, Taste of Dixie Diner, since 2011. We have 8 children, 18 grandchildren, and 3 great-grandchildren. My family is my pride and joy. Most of our time is spent hunting, fishing, and camping! We love the outdoors.
Work History
I began working at the age of 16 at our local TG&Y for Terry Dembo after school and on weekends, and that is where I learned the importance of customer service. All my adult life, I continued in the retail business.
I worked at Piggly Wiggly for Jerry Fulford and then managed a convenience store for several years before going into the banking world.
In 2002, I went to work for the Gilchrist County Clerk of Court and Comptroller under Joe Gilliam and later Todd Newton, where I spent 18 ½ years as a deputy clerk.
I was always told that it’s not a job when you love what you do, and I truly did.
Becoming the Clerk
I was approached in late 2019 about running for Dixie County Clerk of Court & Comptroller, and after careful consideration and prayers, I decided to do just that.
It was not something I took lightly, but I believed I could make a difference if elected. I ran a campaign during COVID-19, which made things difficult. I made the best of it, though. I masked up and went door to door to as many houses as I could over 11 months. I have never been a public speaker; it terrified me, but I did it! I can honestly say I’ve never worked harder at anything in my life. I was blessed to be elected in November of 2020. I took office on January 5, 2021. I gathered my team together and told them what I expected of them:
Transparency, Accountability, Efficiency, and above all else, Customer Service!
My team and I worked hard those first 4 years getting the office up to speed with the help of several other Clerk’s offices (Citrus, Gilchrist, Levy, and Martin), and we are proud of all we accomplished. We continue to work hard for you every day! We are Public Servants!
Goal of the Clerk’s Office
The goal of the Dixie County Clerk’s Office is to efficiently and effectively perform the following:
Clerk of the Circuit and County Courts
Clerk to the Board of County Commissioners
Recorder and Guardian of Public Records
Treasurer, Auditor, and Custodian of all County Funds
The Office of the Clerk of the Circuit Court envisions earning the public trust through leadership in its diverse role as Clerk to the Courts, Guardian of Public Records, and Auditor of the Public Resources and Systems. The Clerk’s Office will be an advocate for people in need of access to public resources and records. We will provide an efficient, friendly, and professional workforce prepared to meet changing customer needs. The Clerk’s Office will safeguard and enhance resources through strong internal audits and effective investment strategies.

Welcome to the Dixie County Florida Property Appraiser's Office
2025 Notice of Certification of Tax Rolls
ATTENTION
If you have experienced storm damage to your home, building or other structure we need to know about it.
As our community works to recover from the recent hurricanes that have damaged our homes and businesses, I want you all to know that my office stands ready to assist you in any way possible. 
We know this is a very difficult time for you and your family. In order to help us assess all damaged property in our county correctly we need you to contact our office, so we can inspect your 
property to properly reassess it for the 2025 Tax Roll. We also can assist you with any 2024 property tax refunds that you may be entitled to. Again, if we can assist you in any way, please call our 
office at 352-498-1212.
Robert A. Lee, CFA
Dixie County Property Appraiser
Dixie County's Property Appraiser is primarily responsible for locating, identifying, and valuing all property within the county for ad valorem tax purposes. 
He is also responsible for administering exemptions, mapping all parcels and classifying agricultural lands. Being custodian of certain county records, he must 
maintain property record cards, subdivision plats, ownership maps, sales data records and prior tax rolls. From these records, one can access our files, determine
 building size, a description of its components, and property characteristics.

Notice to the public

The Code of Judicial Conduct governing behavior by judges forbids judges from discussing pending cases with the public or parties to cases. Please do not call the Court expecting to speak with a judge about any case. The Court is only allowed to consider evidence and arguments made in the courtroom and in documents properly filed by actual parties in the case as authorized by law and the Rules of Court. The Court cannot ethically read or consider any other evidence or arguments about the case.  Ex parte communications also applies to the General Magistrate & Hearing Officers.

Barbie Higginbotham, Clerk of the Circuit Court & Comptroller for Dixie County, Florida
was elected as the Clerk of the Circuit Court & Comptroller on November 2020. The Clerk of the Circuit Court is an elected office established according to the Florida Constitution for the purpose of serving the citizens of each county as a public trustee. As an elected official, the Clerk of the Circuit Court helps provide for the system of “checks and balances” that is the very foundation of the American form of government.
